chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah from 'Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Zurarah from one of the Imams (peace be upon them) who said:

I asked him about the nights in which it is recommended to perform the ritual bath (ghusl) during the month of Ramadan, so he said: 'The night of the nineteenth, the night of the twenty-first, and the night of the twenty-third.'
And he said: 'In the night of the nineteenth, the delegation of the pilgrims is recorded, and in it every wise matter is distinguished (decided).'

And the night of the twenty-first - in it Jesus (peace be upon him) was raised, and in it the successor of Moses (peace be upon him) was taken, and in it the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was taken.

And the night of the twenty-third - and it is the Night of the Juhani, and his narration is that he said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'Indeed, my dwelling is far from the city, so order me to a night in which I may enter.' So he ordered him to the night of the twenty-third.'

And we have previously mentioned in the Book of Prayer, in the chapter on the practices of the month of Ramadan, what is recommended for a person to say from supplication and recitation of the Quran, so there is no need to repeat it here, and it is sufficient, God willing.
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended nights for ritual bath (ghusl) in Ramadan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* identifies the 19th, 21st, and 23rd nights of Ramadan as the 'Nights of Ghusl,' linking them to the martyrdom of Imam Ali (AS) and the ascension of Prophet Jesus (AS). It specifically highlights the 23rd night as the 'Night of the Juhani,' referencing a tradition where the Prophet advised a companion to enter Medina on this night, thereby establishing its distinct ritual significance in Shia jurisprudence.
